hyperedges.label: The three-file output of a graphify run
Team workflow: commit graphify-out, auto-rebuild, conflict-free merges

nodes.label: /graphify skill command
nodes.rationale: Invoked from inside the AI coding assistant so the model API is supplied by the IDE session — no extra API keys needed.

nodes.label: graphifyy PyPI package
nodes.rationale: Published as graphifyy (double y) while the CLI command stays graphify; other graphify* PyPI packages are unrelated. uvx graphify fails because uv tool run reads the first word as a package name, so --from graphifyy is required.

nodes.label: uv tool install
nodes.rationale: Recommended over plain pip because it isolates the package in its own environment, avoiding ModuleNotFoundError when the skill's runtime Python differs from pip's target environment.

nodes.label: pipx install
nodes.rationale: Alternative isolated installer; same isolation benefit as uv tool install.

nodes.label: graphify install
nodes.rationale: Bare `graphify install` stays single-platform (Claude Code) on purpose; use --platform agents when the skill should be visible to every framework reading .agents/skills.

nodes.label: graphify install --project
nodes.rationale: Writes skill files into the current repo instead of the user profile so they can be committed.

nodes.label: graphify extract (headless extraction)
nodes.rationale: Auto-detects the provider from whichever key is set (Gemini -> Kimi -> Claude -> OpenAI -> DeepSeek -> Azure -> Bedrock -> Ollama).

nodes.label: graphify query
nodes.rationale: Preferred over reading the full report or grepping raw files because targeted queries are cheaper and more focused.

nodes.label: graphify hook install
nodes.rationale: Embeds the current interpreter path directly into the hook scripts at install time so post-commit rebuilds work in GUI git clients and CI where ~/.local/bin is not on PATH; re-run after upgrading to refresh the embedded path.

nodes.label: graphify reflect
nodes.rationale: --if-stale makes it cheap enough to run every session by doing nothing when LESSONS.md is newer than all inputs.

nodes.label: Working-memory learning layer (.graphify_learning.json)
nodes.rationale: Tags nodes preferred/tentative/contested with recency weighting and provenance, and marks lessons 'code changed — re-verify' when the source moved on.

nodes.label: graphify prs (PR dashboard, triage, conflicts)
nodes.rationale: --conflicts surfaces PRs sharing graph communities because those carry merge-order risk.

nodes.label: graphify export callflow-html
nodes.rationale: Produces a readable architecture page with Mermaid call-flow diagrams; regenerates automatically on each commit when the hook is installed.

nodes.label: python -m graphify.serve (MCP server)
nodes.rationale: Exposes the graph as structured MCP tools so the assistant gets repeatable tool access instead of ad-hoc file reads.

nodes.label: MCP tools (query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, shortest_path, list_prs, get_pr_impact, triage_prs)
MCP Streamable HTTP transport
nodes.rationale: Lets one shared process serve the graph to the whole team so clients point their IDE MCP config at a URL instead of running graphify locally; default host 127.0.0.1 is loopback-only, and exposing beyond localhost requires --host 0.0.0.0 together with --api-key.

nodes.label: graphify-out/ output directory
nodes.rationale: Meant to be committed to git so every teammate starts with a ready-made map.

nodes.label: graph.json
nodes.rationale: The full graph, queryable at any moment without re-reading the files.

nodes.label: graph.html visualization
nodes.rationale: Skip generation above ~5000 nodes because the HTML becomes too large for a browser to open.

nodes.label: GRAPH_REPORT.md
nodes.rationale: Kept for broad architecture review even when targeted queries are preferred for specific questions.

nodes.label: manifest.json
nodes.rationale: Keys are stored as relative paths and re-anchored on load, making it portable and safe to commit — which saves a full rebuild on first checkout.

nodes.label: git merge driver for graph.json
nodes.rationale: Configured by hook install so two developers committing in parallel get an automatic union-merge and graph.json is never left with conflict markers.

nodes.label: .graphifyignore
nodes.rationale: Merged with .gitignore and evaluated last so its patterns win on conflict; it can only exclude more, never re-include a file .gitignore already excluded.

nodes.label: tree-sitter AST extraction (36 grammars)
nodes.rationale: Code is parsed locally with no API calls, so nothing leaves the machine and a code-only corpus needs no API key.

nodes.label: LLM semantic extraction (docs, PDF, images)
nodes.rationale: Documents, PDFs and images require an LLM call, so empty nodes/edges for them signal a missing API key or wrong backend.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md instruction file
nodes.rationale: On platforms without payload-bearing hooks (e.g. Trae), persistent instruction files are the durable mechanism that delivers the same graph-first guidance.

nodes.label: PreToolUse hook
nodes.rationale: Fires before search-style tool calls (and Read/Glob on Claude Code) to steer the assistant to graphify query instead of grepping raw files.

nodes.label: .cursor/rules/graphify.mdc
nodes.rationale: Written with alwaysApply: true so Cursor includes it in every conversation automatically, removing the need for a hook.

nodes.label: .kilo/plugins/graphify.js (tool.execute.before plugin)
nodes.rationale: Gives Kilo the same persistent graph-reminder behaviour through native .kilo configuration.

nodes.label: Codex
nodes.rationale: Requires multi_agent = true under [features] in ~/.codex/config.toml for parallel extraction, and uses $graphify instead of /graphify.

nodes.label: CodeBuddy
nodes.rationale: Uses the same Agent tool and PreToolUse hook mechanism as Claude Code.

nodes.label: Trae
nodes.rationale: Launches subagents in parallel via the Agent tool but does not support PreToolUse hooks, so AGENTS.md is the durable mechanism there.

nodes.label: Aider
nodes.rationale: Uses serial extraction because parallel-agent support is still early on this platform.

nodes.label: OpenClaw
nodes.rationale: Uses serial extraction because parallel-agent support is still early on this platform.

nodes.label: Factory Droid
nodes.rationale: Uses the Task tool to launch subagents in parallel.

nodes.label: Agent Skills (cross-platform .agents/skills)
nodes.rationale: Targets the generic ~/.agents/skills and ./.agents/skills locations so any spec-compliant framework can read the skill.

nodes.label: --backend openai (OpenAI-compatible)
nodes.rationale: Preferred over the Ollama layer for cloud gateways like OpenRouter because it is a cleaner OpenAI-compatible path.

nodes.label: --backend ollama (local)
nodes.rationale: Recommended for code with data-residency requirements because it is fully local.

nodes.label: --backend bedrock (AWS Bedrock)
nodes.rationale: Uses the standard IAM credential chain rather than an API key.

nodes.label: --backend kimi (Moonshot)
nodes.rationale: Routes to Moonshot AI servers in China — a data-residency consideration.

nodes.label: GRAPHIFY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS
nodes.rationale: Raised for dense corpora so the model's JSON reply does not hit the output ceiling and get truncated mid-string.

nodes.label: GRAPHIFY_FORCE / --force
nodes.rationale: Needed because a refactor that deletes files leaves stale nodes behind; --force overrides the guard that rejects a smaller rebuild.

nodes.label: GRAPHIFY_OLLAMA_NUM_CTX
nodes.rationale: The KV-cache window is auto-tuned but can exceed the GPU's VRAM, so it can be lowered manually.

nodes.label: --token-budget
nodes.rationale: Smaller inputs produce smaller outputs; the reliable lever when the model has its own output ceiling.

nodes.label: Query log (~/.cache/graphify-queries.log)
nodes.rationale: Records timestamp, question, corpus, returned nodes and duration as JSON Lines; full subgraph responses are not stored by default.

nodes.label: Privacy posture (no telemetry, local-first)
nodes.rationale: No telemetry, no usage tracking, no analytics; code and audio/video stay on the machine.

nodes.label: Confidence tags (EXTRACTED / INFERRED / AMBIGUOUS)
nodes.rationale: Every inferred relationship is labelled so you always know what was found versus what was guessed.

nodes.label: Surprising connections
nodes.rationale: Links between things living in different files or modules, ranked by surprisal.

nodes.label: The WHY nodes (NOTE/WHY/HACK comments, docstrings, design rationale)
nodes.rationale: Extracted as separate nodes linked to the code they explain, so design intent is queryable alongside structure.

nodes.label: Suggested questions
nodes.rationale: 4-5 questions the graph is uniquely positioned to answer.

nodes.label: graphifyy[video] extra (faster-whisper + yt-dlp)
nodes.rationale: Transcription runs locally with faster-whisper so audio/video never leaves the machine.

nodes.label: Google Workspace extraction (--google-workspace, gws CLI)
nodes.rationale: .gdoc/.gsheet/.gslides files are shortcuts rather than document content, so graphify exports them to graphify-out/converted/ as companion Markdown before extracting.

nodes.label: --obsidian vault export
nodes.rationale: Never overwrites your existing notes or .obsidian configuration when writing into an existing vault.

nodes.label: --wiki markdown wiki
nodes.rationale: Built so agents can crawl it.

nodes.label: Ghost duplicate node merging
nodes.rationale: The same symbol appears twice — once from AST extraction with a source location, once from semantic extraction without one — so builds now merge them automatically; graphs built before v0.8.33 need a full re-extract.

nodes.label: Package manifest extraction (pyproject.toml, go.mod, pom.xml, apm.yml)
nodes.rationale: One canonical package node per package name plus depends_on edges, so a package referenced from several manifests forms a single hub.
